correctness.rationale: Arbitrary real-linear extensions are reduced without loss by signed-permutation averaging to coefficient rows (a,b,c). In dimension three two explicit 1-Lipschitz test potentials give intersecting universal affine bounds, attained by a nonnegative row. In higher dimensions an incident-vertex test and two disjoint-edge KR/transport bounds have a positive convex combination equal to the claimed constant, and the indicated nonnegative kernel attains it across all pair orbits. The precise geometric distances and finite orbit census are explicit in RESULT.md. Direct linear programming separately checked all 4430 pairs in dimensions 3–6. Computation is not an infinite proof; no uniqueness is claimed.

originality.rationale: The sharp complete edge-midpoint extension constants for cross-polytope vertices, with the discrete dimension-three/four change in active metric pairs, were not found in the accessible previous exact claims or the inspected general Lipschitz extension full texts. The signed-permutation/optimal-transport framework is prior art, not claimed as new. A regular simplex has equilateral initial-vertex distances and is neither equivalent to nor implies the antipodal cross-polytope calculation.
residual_risks: An equivalent exact finite-metric interpolation computation may appear in less well-indexed Lipschitz-free or polytope interpolation literature.

value.rationale: An explicit all-dimensional optimum for a natural mesh-refinement/stable interpolation problem, with a sharp geometric regime change when disjoint coordinate-support edges first occur. The exact optimal positive kernels improve ordinary midpoint interpolation and identify a nontrivial limiting loss 4-2 sqrt(2), providing reusable extremal finite-metric benchmarks. This is more than an arbitrary small-case calculation.
